newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil reclaims gold mine and reassures investors.
newsitem.headline: Brazil reclaims gold mine and reassures investors.

text.p: The Brazilian government's move to reclaim a huge gold deposit in northern Brazil from wildcat miners has secured the mine and sent a reassuring signal to prospective overseas investors, officials and analysts said.

After surveys at the Serra Leste mine have been halted by gold diggers for many months, troops and federal police moved into the area on Thursday, arresting nine people in an operation which officials said passed without bloodshed.
"The government had to act with prudence, as well as firmness," said independent gold consultant Paulo Cesar de Moraes Sarmento.
"This operation is very important. It creates a more peaceful climate for investors and assures them of greater legal security," Sarmento said.
Since May, hundreds of "garimpeiros", as freelance gold prospectors are called in Brazil, have blocked survey work at the mine in the Amazonian state of Para.

As a result, state mining company Companhia Vale do Rio Doce (CVRD) which owns the mining rights to Serra Leste suffered losses of $100,000 a day and has been prevented from evaluating the true extent of the deposit.

At an international gold conference in Rio de Janeiro in August, prospective overseas mining investors voiced concern about the situation in Serra Leste and were watching to see how the government would resolve the impasse.
"I think this is positive for Brazil...as we have guaranteed the rights of the mining companies," said Miguel Navarrete Fernandez, director general of the National Mineral Production Department.
CVRD's manager of precious metal projects, Helcio Guerra, said the company was already preparing to resume work as soon as possible and that surveys could resume by the end of this week.
The impasse has not been without a cost. CVRD has lost around eight months and the company will now only be in a position next year to confirm the estimated 150 tonnes of reserves.
News in February of the Serra Leste gold discovery came at an ideal time for the government which is privatizing CVRD in February next year.
The deposit is seen as having great pulling power in attracting large investors and enhancing the value of the company.

The garimpeiros however also want a share of Serra Leste's future profits, claiming it is an extension of the former opencast Serra Pelada gold mine, the site of the biggest gold rush in history to which they had the mining rights.
CVRD, however, took the matter to court and had its mining rights in Serra Leste reconfirmed.
"We are very happy about the re-establishment of the state of democracy in the region," Guerra said.
CVRD hopes to start production of 15 tonnes annually by the year 2000. A CVRD spokeswoman said it was too early to forecast turnover once the $250 million mining project was up and running.

CVRD already owns the largest existing gold mine in Brazil in Igarape Bahia, also in Para, which produces 10 out of total CVRD gold output of 18.2 tonnes. By the year 2000, CVRD hopes to increase annual production to 31 tonnes.
Total Brazilian production is seen at up to 70 tonnes this year.
-- Simona de Logu, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 507 4151
